stem: A radio station in Dhaka asked its listeners to send a text message saying whether they support or oppose a plan to build a new flyover in the city. Of the 3,200 listeners who sent a message, 85% said they oppose the plan. Which of the following best explains why this result should NOT be used to estimate the percent of all Dhaka residents who oppose the plan?

choices.A: A result as high as 85% cannot be accurate for any survey.
choices.B: A sample of 3,200 people is too small to represent a large city.
choices.C: The results of a survey can never be applied to people who were not surveyed.
choices.D: The listeners chose whether to respond, so the people who sent messages may not represent all residents.

solution: Only listeners who felt like texting were counted: a voluntary response sample.
People with strong opinions, and people who listen to this station, are more likely to respond, so the sample may not represent all residents.

explanation.A: Incorrect. A high percent is not a sign of error; it is how the sample was chosen that matters.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Size is not the problem; even a very large voluntary response sample can be biased.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Results from a random sample can be applied to the population it was drawn from.
explanation.D: Correct. A voluntary response sample is not random, so it may over-represent people with strong opinions.

verify:
choices = {o: choices[n] for o, n in {'C': 'A', 'A': 'B', 'D': 'C', 'B': 'D'}.items()}; answer = {'A': 'C', 'B': 'A', 'C': 'D', 'D': 'B'}[answer]  # shuffled: original letters
design = {'random_sample': False, 'self_selected': True, 'n': 3200}
assert design['self_selected'] and not design['random_sample']
ok = [k for k, v in choices.items() if 'chose whether to respond' in v]
assert ok == [answer]
